text.p: These are the leading stories in the Belgrade press on Friday. Reuters has not verified them nor does it vouch for their accuracy.
NASA BORBA
- Over 150,000 demonstrators in Belgrade protest against partial annulment of local election results and celebrate St. Nikolas' day. Opposition protests continue in other Serbian towns.
- Belgrade students, joined by students from Kragujevac, continue protests demanding respect of democratic election results.
- Ruling Socialist Party of Serbia (SPS) supporters stage rallies of support to Serbian President Slobodan Milosevic in Krusevac, Pozarevac, Sabac and other towns in Serbia.
- Independent trade union Nezavisnost calls on its members and other trade unions to stage a protest outside the Serbian parliament on Tuesday, December 24.
- Yugoslav federal government submits 1997 draft budget of 9.23 billion dinars ($1.8 billion) to federal parliament for adoption.

- Yugoslav finance minister Tomica Raicevic to meet representatives of the Bank of International Settlements in Basle. Nasa Borba unofficially learns Yugoslavia has agreed to the division of former Yugoslavia's gold deposited in the bank separately from the rest of the former federation's assets.
- Organisation for Security and Cooperation in Europe (OSCE) delegation due in Belgrade to examine dispute over local elections which has provoked several weeks of demonstrations throughout Serbia.
- Danielle Mitterrand, the wife of late French President Francois Mitterand, to visit Belgrade and hold a disucssion on December 22 on the topic "Culture, freedom of the media and human rights".
POLITIKA
- Yugoslav Foreign Minister Milan Milutinovic says OSCE team invited to Belgrade to be informed of relevant facts regarding local elections.

- Foreign firms are showing great interest in Yugoslav infrastructure development projects but some solutions are being postponed over present internal situation caused by "irresponsible people in the country", says Serbian minister coordinator Dragan Tomic.
- Yugoslav airlines JAT expects total revenue in 1997 to be over $220 million.
- The new labour relations law will take into account trade union requests for protection of surplus workers.
- The Serbian parliament to discuss the 1997 budget at its session on December 24.
VECERNJE NOVOSTI
- Serbian Justice Ministry to publish by Saturday expertise about the legality of the annulment of local election results in Nis.
- Montenegrin finance minister Predrag Goranovic says state funds on private accounts abroad are strictly controlled by the government, documentation exists for all transactions.
BORBA
- Projects for building trans-Yugoslav highway and railroad infrastructure ready, works to begin next spring, Serbian government transport and communications coordination team says.
- Federal government adopts several foreign trade acts further liberalising imports of industrial equipment.
- Bosna shoe factory from Banja Luka renews cooperation with Germany's Salamander for processing customer supplied goods. -- Belgrade newsroom +381 11 2224305
